column1:
Hawkish core with tempered edge. The FOMC delivered a 75 bp hike to 2.25–2.50%, signaled “ongoing increases,” and continued balance sheet runoff with caps stepping up in September ($60B Treasuries, $35B MBS). The statement remains inflation-first despite acknowledging softer spending/production.

Beige Book context slightly moderates the hawkish take:
- Across multiple Districts, banks report increased usage of revolving credit lines, suggesting tighter financial conditions and precautionary liquidity use by firms.
- Residential loan demand is weakening broadly, aligning with higher rates and housing deceleration.
- Together with SLOOS-reported tightening in C&I/CRE standards and selected residential categories, bank credit supply is constricting, adding a non-Fed drag on growth.

Net: still clearly hawkish given the explicit guidance for further hikes and accelerated QT, but Beige Book and SLOOS evidence of tightening credit and softer housing temper the path-of-policy aggressiveness at the margin.
